title: Bishkek to Ysyk-Kol's south shore
desc: You head out from Bishkek toward the lakes, stopping first at the Burana Tower, an 11th-century minaret standing alone on the steppe, all that's left of a Silk Road town, with old stone carvings dotted around it. Lunch is with a Dungan family in Iskra Village, whose food mixes Chinese and Central Asian traditions in a way you won't taste anywhere else.

From there the road follows the southern shore of Ysyk-Kol, the huge lake at the heart of the region. In the late afternoon you stop at the Fairy-Tale canyons, where wind and water have shaped the rock into odd, castle-like forms, before settling into a guesthouse in Bokonbaev Village.

title: Eagle hunter & the climb to Song-Kol
desc: The day starts with a local eagle hunter, who shows how these golden eagles are trained and flown, a skill handed down through the family for generations. From Bokonbaev you drive on to Kochkor Village for lunch and a short break.

The road then climbs into the mountains over the Kalmak-Ashuu Pass at 3400 m and brings you down to Song-Kol, a high lake ringed by summer pastures. There's time for a walk along the shore before dinner, and you spend the night in a traditional yurt; pack warm layers, as it gets cold once the sun drops.
meals: breakfast & lunch at guesthouse, dinner at yurt

title: Song-Kol ride & return to Bishkek
desc: After breakfast there's the option of an easy ride around the lake, passing yurts and grazing herds at a gentle pace, relaxed enough for anyone new to the saddle. Lunch is back at the yurt before you set off home.

The drive back to Bishkek crosses the Tuz-Ashuu Pass and runs down through the Kilemche pastures, with mountain views the whole way. It's a long day on the road, but a fitting last look at the high country before you reach the city.
